newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: France tells Czechs it promoting EU, NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: France tells Czechs it promoting EU, NATO expansion.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Friday his country was ready to accelerate the process of European Union and NATO enlargement, adding he backed Czech aspirations to join the EU by the year 2000.

"France is determined to support and even accelerate all processes concerning enlargement of the EU and the Atlantic alliance. We consider that it is a strategic choice which is important for European unity, not only for current members but also for candidates," de Charette told a joint news conference with Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec.
The Czech Republic is a leading candidate for early membership in both the EU and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

"I think it would be realistic to talk about the end of our negotiations with the EU at the end of the millenium. The new millenium would have for us not only a symbolic but a practical value," Zieleniec told the news conference.
To which De Charette said: "I entirely agree."
De Charette, on a two-day visit to the Czech capital, said he was also in Prague to prepare for a visit of French President Jacques Chirac at the beginning of April.

At the end of a two-day visit to Hungary on Friday, Chirac stood by a forecast he made at the start of his trip on Thursday that the first wave of admissions to the EU, including that of Hungary, should take place by 2000.

Speaking at a joint news conference with Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn in Budapest, he also warned that the enlargement of NATO must be well prepared in advance with full consultation with all sides and with due regard for Russia's sensitivities.
"(The enlargement) must be done in a way which does not give Russia the sentiment of being humiliated or confronted," Chirac said.
